title: How to Think Like a Roman Emperor

questions.q: What does living virtuously mean for the Stoics?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says virtue means accepting your condition and living in agreement with nature.

questions.q: Which four virtues does the summary call the Stoic core?
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists wisdom, morality, courage and moderation as the four cardinal virtues.

questions.q: How does the summary say the virtues are mastered?
questions.why: Lesson 2 says practice is repeated action, and results come from acting on the principles.

questions.q: What should you do about things you cannot control?
questions.why: Lesson 3 says it is pointless to worry about what you cannot change, so accept it.

questions.q: How did Marcus Aurelius approach death?
a: He acknowledged it and made the most of his days
He sought a way to become immortal
He refused to think about it at all
He feared it and withdrew from ruling
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he accepted death as inevitable instead of dwelling on it.
